articles.title_orig: Eric Trump-partnered Robotics CEO addresses 'Terminator' fears as he sends combat humanoids into warzones
articles.title_zh: Eric Trump-partnered Robotics CEO addresses 'Terminator' fears as he sends combat humanoids into warzones
articles.content_orig:
Emily covers breaking news from all over the world. She previously reported on home news and politics for The Telegraph. You can reach her at emily.smith@telegraph.co.uk
An Eric Trump-backed firm is in talks to send 1,000 humanoid robots into the tunnels under Gaza.
Foundation Future Industries said it was in direct talks with senior Israeli military officials to deploy its Phantom MK1 robot to patrol Hamas tunnels in the strip.
The IDF is expected to purchase up to 1,000 robots from the company, where Donald Trump’s son was named chief strategic adviser in March.
The robots, capable of engaging in combat, neutralising booby traps and detecting trip wires, cost around $150,000 (£115,000) per unit.
Mike LeBlanc, the company’s co-founder and president, told the Financial Times : “We’re in direct talks with the chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces.”
He said that the president’s son was “very mechanically inclined”, adding: “He [Eric Trump] loves talking about the robots, he loves asking questions about the robots... He’s been very valuable as an adviser.”
Leading US robotics firms have promised that their products will not be used for military combat.
Mr LeBlanc said there was “no question... of building a ‘Terminator’”.
But he added: “Is anybody sitting around and debating heat-seeking missiles? Because they’re pretty scary and they’re pretty autonomous.
“If you can keep somebody from having to kick in a door not knowing if there’s an enemy on the other side with a gun pointed at it, that’s kind of the highest purpose of what these robots could do.”
In February 2026, two Phantom MK1 robot units were reportedly sent to Ukraine for front-line reconnaissance, resupply and logistical evaluation.
If the deal is reached, the robots will be sent to patrol the Hamas-controlled tunnels beneath Gaza , which span around 300 miles.
Mr Trump, 42, holds an equity stake in Foundation Future Industries, which was founded in 2024.
Mr LeBlanc said the company had received more than $70m (£53m) in contracts from the US military.
A spokesman for Mr Trump said the president’s son had “no involvement in Foundation’s management, operations, strategic decisions or commercial activities, including the solicitation, negotiation, procurement or execution of any government contracts”.
They added in a statement to the Financial Times that Mr Trump had “never introduced Foundation to any government agency or participated in any government contract negotiations. All contracting decisions are made independently by Foundation’s management without his involvement or influence.”
Mr LeBlanc claimed Mr Trump’s involvement had no part in securing the contract. However, he said he expected to be called to testify before Congress himself.
On The IDF claims, a Foundation Future Industries spokesman said: “Foundation Future Industries is not working with the Israel Defense Forces and has not supplied any robots to the IDF.
“Foundation has no contract or other agreement with the IDF or the Israeli Ministry of Defense. No Foundation robots have been sold, delivered or deployed to the IDF.
“Any conversations mentioned in the report were early and exploratory. They did not lead to an agreement. We’ve had no conversations with the IDF in any official capacity and Foundation is not negotiating to supply the IDF.”
The award of government contracts to companies with links to the Trump family has drawn fierce criticism.
Last month, The Telegraph uncovered several conflicts of interest in the president’s board of peace (BoP), the US body charged with ending the war in Gaza.
Jared Kushner, the United States Special Envoy for Peace and board executive on the BoP, owns Affinity Partners, a firm which holds a major stake in Phoenix Financial, a Tel Aviv insurance and investment business that in turn invests in a series of companies linked to the Israeli military.
The Telegraph found that one of those companies – a small Israeli defence firm called Smart Shooter Ltd – last month beat off competition from more established players to win a US military contract worth up to $150m (£114m).

articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on Thursday, November 19 , and you can preload the game on your PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S starting today, Rockstar Games has announced. The studio has also revealed what kind of visuals players can expect on their respective consoles, making clear that regardless of where you play, GTA VI targets 30 FPS gameplay.
"Grand Theft Auto VI has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits to bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life – while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants," Rockstar writes in a blog post .
Rockstar Games also breaks down the different graphical settings available on PlayStation and Xbox consoles. On PS5 Pro, GTA VI will feature "improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro." On PS5 and PS5 Pro, the game will include "high-fidelity haptic feedback" fully integrated into DualSense controllers and adjustable via accessibility settings, improved spatial rendering so all in-game sounds take full advantage of Tempest 3D audio, and improved load times, "making Grand Theft Auto VI play best on PlayStation 5 consoles."
On Xbox consoles, Rockstar doesn't dive into performance; instead, it focuses on Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox Series X/S and Xbox One consoles, noting this feature will use Xbox Series S graphics settings.
GTA VI will also fully support Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox.
GTA VI launches November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.
For more, check out the song "Pusher" from the game's original score , then check out the GTA VI launch trailer . After that, check out this exclusive story about how GTA VI features over 170 animal species and another about its tropical storms and hurricanes .

articles.title_orig: Ukraine launches nearly 1,200 drones at Russia as US-led talks will consider wider European security
articles.title_zh: Ukraine launches nearly 1,200 drones at Russia as US-led talks will consider wider European security
articles.content_orig:
Ukraine has launched nearly 1,200 drones at Russian targets in one of its largest aerial attacks since the invasion began almost five years ago
KYIV, Ukraine -- Ukraine fired almost 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its biggest aerial attacks since Moscow’s invasion nearly five years ago.
Meanwhile, U.S. and Russian negotiators raised the stakes in talks to stop the fighting by including for discussion wider European security arrangements that have been in place since the end of the Cold War. That change, long sought by Moscow, has alarmed European leaders and placed a question mark over NATO’s future role.
“Russia wants to talk about questions of European security architecture. We don’t need to talk about that. There is one,” German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said, referring to the NATO military alliance.
After two days of talks with Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi this week, U.S. envoys went in person to brief Russian President Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who was meeting with European leaders in Dublin, Ireland.
Further talks are planned as negotiators seek a breakthrough in peace efforts, according to U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also President Donald Trump’s son-in-law.
Kushner said Russia has agreed to include Europe in upcoming talks, after Moscow's long insistence that the continent’s governments should be excluded because they were part of the problem by supporting Ukraine.
Europe’s presence at the negotiating table will allow negotiators “to address the broader postwar European security arrangements alongside the territorial issues between Ukraine and Russia,” Kushner said on X.
As European leaders scrambled to find an envoy to the talks, they were also wary of Russian maneuvering as well as Trump’s praise for Putin and his administration’s sharp criticism of Europe .
The EU’s top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said Friday that Europe must insist on a ceasefire before taking the negotiations further — the opposite of what Putin demands .
“If we start to talk about what Russia is asking regarding the security architecture, we actually walk into the traps that Russia is setting us,” she said in Dublin.
Luxembourg Prime Minister Luc Frieden insisted that Europe must take its fate into its own hands. “We cannot let neither the Americans nor the Russians decide about our future,” Frieden said.
Moscow is aiming “to dismantle NATO and the post-Cold War European security architecture,” the Institute for the Study of War said in an assessment late Thursday.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov reaffirmed that Russia is open for contacts with the Europeans.
“Once we understand (Europe’s) true intentions and their readiness to facilitate the peace process, then it will be possible to make a decision on holding a dialogue regarding a settlement in Ukraine in an expanded format,” Peskov said.
Zelenskyy on Friday repeated his complaints about drone speed limits on the U.S. Starshield system — SpaceX’s military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service — that Ukraine needs for its defense.
The speed restrictions are limiting Ukrainian drones to 161 kph (100 mph) on the entire front line and in Russian-occupied territory, he said, making it impossible for Ukraine to deploy its interceptors effectively against Russia's fast-moving jet-powered drones.
“We still have no clear explanations,” he said of the unannounced restrictions, after first raising the issue on Thursday.
Ukrainian officials are asking the U.S. Department of State, the Pentagon and SpaceX to clarify and resolve the situation, he said.
Last month, similar SpaceX limits on Ukrainian drone speeds severely disrupted operations, alarming Kyiv officials who fear a drop in U.S. support.
Elon Musk acknowledged in October that his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink internet service in Ukraine for about a week, saying the system couldn’t be used for offensive strikes against Russia.
Russia’s Defense Ministry said air defenses downed 1,198 Ukrainian long-range drones between late Thursday and early Friday. However, strikes on three Russian regions killed seven people, including a 12-year-old, and wounded 17, local officials said.
The massive Ukrainian barrage appeared designed to show that Kyiv is holding its own in the war, countering Moscow’s insistence that a Russian victory is inevitable.
Kyiv’s forces are using drones and ground robots to help defend against Russia’s army along the about 1,200-kilometer (750-mile) front line snaking down eastern and southeastern Ukraine.
With its troops largely bogged down on the battlefield, Moscow has used strategic bombardment of civilian areas to hurt Ukraine.
Russia launched 117 drones against Ukraine overnight, killing at least two people, including a 17-year-old, authorities said.
A single Russian attack on southern Zaporizhzhia on Friday hit two five-story apartment blocks and wounded 25 people, including six children, officials said.
The war has killed hundreds of thousands of soldiers and thousands of civilians, analysts and humanitarian organizations say.
Russian attacks against Ukraine’s energy infrastructure caused widespread power outages across about half of the country's regions Friday, First Deputy Minister of Energy Artem Nekrasov said.
Moscow has battered Ukraine’s power grid each winter since the war began, hoping to weaken public morale.
AP reporters Sam McNeil in Dublin, Susie Blann in Kyiv, Ukraine and Barry Hatton in Lisbon, Portugal contributed to this story.

articles.title_orig: Scoop: Israeli spy chief in D.C. as Netanyahu presses Trump to resume war
articles.title_zh: Scoop: Israeli spy chief in D.C. as Netanyahu presses Trump to resume war
articles.content_orig:
Despite losing its majority in last month’s parliamentary elections, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government is still in power in a caretaker capacity.
That will continue until a new governing majority is formed – a process that could take months as Israel’s opposition struggles to form a coalition.
And while he may be politically weakened, Netanyahu is reported to be weighing new military action against Iran , despite a lack of enthusiasm from the United States, his own military establishment, and the politicians vying to replace him.
But does Netanyahu’s caretaker government actually have the authority to send Israel back to war, and how would such a move be received at home?
Officially, Israel’s caretaker government has the same authority as a regular government. Article 30 of the country’s Basic Law states that an interim government continues to carry out the same duties until a new one takes its place.
However, Israel’s Supreme Court has previously ruled that an outgoing government must avoid irreversible policy moves unless they are urgent – a principle known as the “duty of restraint”.
In practice, Netanyahu can still initiate military action with the approval of his caretaker government, which he could present as “urgent and in the national interest”, Neve Gordon, a professor of international law at Queen Mary University, London, and the author of “Israel’s Occupation”, told Al Jazeera.
Or Asher, a researcher at the Tel Aviv-based Tachlith Institute, told the Reuters news agency that security issues generally are “the clearest exception” to a caretaker government’s duty of restraint.
“The Supreme Court has historically avoided intervening in decisions to go to war, and parliamentary oversight is at its thinnest in the weeks after the new Knesset [parliament] ⁠⁠convenes and before its committees are formed,” said Asher.
“A caretaker prime minister can legally take Israel to war, including against Iran,” he added.
Ehab Jabareen, an analyst and Palestinian citizen of Israel, told Al Jazeera the government’s caretaker status raises the “political burden of proof”.
“Netanyahu would be asking the country to accept the consequences of a decision that could outlast his government,” he said.
On Wednesday, Israeli media reported that the security cabinet chaired by Netanyahu had ordered the military to step up preparations for an attack on Iran.
“The directives issued by the security cabinet to the Israeli military could lead it to carry out activities that could trigger a war,” public broadcaster KAN reported.
That followed reports that Netanyahu has been repeatedly calling US President Donald Trump to press for a new military campaign against Iran, conversations that on at least one occasion became heated, according to Israel’s Ynet News site.
On Thursday, a US military official was quoted by KAN as saying that Washington had told Israel to get ready for a potential new round of confrontation. But the US military’s Central Command (CENTCOM) later dismissed the reports, telling Al Jazeera they were “mere speculation”.
According to Israel’s Channel 13, the Israeli military establishment sees no urgent need to attack Iran. It said that assessment had been presented to Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, who has been tasked with forming the next government, during a briefing on Wednesday.
The opposition has demanded that Netanyahu avoid any military action unless it is critical.
Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Lieberman, a member of the opposition bloc, said the prime minister’s caretaker government must not “make decisions that could drag Israel into war without parliamentary oversight and without the full agreement of all security officials”.
Eisenkot echoed this sentiment in a letter to Netanyahu on Wednesday, saying that deploying Israeli forces “without a direct and immediate threat that cannot wait could have devastating consequences for Israeli democracy and public trust in the institutions of government”.
The Israeli premier responded by insisting the government makes all decisions based only on “security considerations”.
There would be serious divisions.
“Obviously, those who voted for Netanyahu and parties from his coalition would be in favour, while most of those who supported the so-called change bloc would be upset at Netanyahu’s use of the war to try to remain in power and block their electoral success,” said Gordon.
But ultimately, he said, most people who voted against Netanyahu’s bloc would “rally around the flag” if he resumes hostilities.
Jabareen agreed that Israelis would likely rally if a new war breaks out and missiles are incoming. But he said that “tells you very little about whether they think Netanyahu was right to start another round [of conflict]”.
“And the harder test comes when reservists are called up again, families are back in shelters and the government has to explain what the campaign can achieve that the previous one didn’t,” he added.
Jabareen said the debate in Israel over any new confrontation on Iran would likely centre on “why now?”
“If the case for urgency is weak, especially if Washington is opposed and senior Israeli commanders have reservations, the decision could be seen as an attempt to change the political agenda while Eisenkot is trying to form a government,” he said.
Beyond domestic considerations, an obstacle to Netanyahu restarting attacks may be the position of Israel’s main ally, the US, which has said it is doubling down on its economic pressure campaign against Iran rather than pursuing more large-scale military action.
“Netanyahu’s problem … is not the Israeli public, but what seems to be a loss of appetite in the US,” said Gordon.
Anders Persson, a political scientist specialising in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, said it would be easier for Netanyahu to pull off a new military campaign if it is undertaken jointly with the US.
But “the more openly Netanyahu provokes Iran, and the less support he receives from Trump, the harder it will be for him to get away with it – and for the Israeli public to accept it”, Persson told Al Jazeera.
Yes. And in one case, the government was led by Netanyahu himself.
In May 2021, weeks after his party lost seats in legislative elections and while negotiations for a new government were under way, the prime minister launched an 11-day war in Gaza that killed at least 260 people in the Palestinian enclave. Thirteen people also died in Israel.
While that conflict temporarily stalled efforts to replace Netanyahu, a new government, led by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, was formed the following month, ending a 12-year run as prime minister .
Former Israeli prime ministers Ehud Olmert and Yair Lapid also ordered military action in Gaza while serving in a caretaker capacity. The 2008 war directed by Olmert was by far the most deadly , killing about 1,400 Palestinians.

articles.title_orig: What's Trump's strategy now with Iran? To keep things as they are
articles.title_zh: What's Trump's strategy now with Iran? To keep things as they are
articles.content_orig:
President Trump says he is leaning toward a new solution to the Iran nuclear crisis: Declare it is over, even if not much has changed.
Mr. Trump and his team have taken to asserting that they have the Iranians right where they want them. They say they no longer need a new nuclear agreement that would remove potential bomb fuel from the country, or to limit Iran’s missile capability, two of the leading reasons the president cited 10 months ago for going to war.
Mr. Trump appears — at least for now — to have rejected a series of military options that would involve intense, if time-limited, attacks on military installations, nuclear sites and even some energy infrastructure.
All the talk this year of sending in commandos to seize roughly 970 pounds of uranium from the country, enriched to a near-bomb-grade level of 60 percent purity, has been abandoned, albeit for the moment. So has the detailed analysis of whether America’s biggest bunker busters are powerful enough to get deep into Pickaxe Mountain, a site U.S. intelligence believes — but is not sure — is the location of advanced centrifuges that can purify uranium into bomb fuel.
In comments to reporters this week in Paris, where he was attending a meeting of foreign ministers from the Group of 7, Secretary of State Marco Rubio described an approach best characterized as strategic patience: waiting for sanctions on Iran to take their toll and ultimately crack their government.
“At this point, the economic campaign and the pressure and the devastation that our economic campaign is having on the Iranian regime is working so well that the president really doesn’t have any need to conduct major combat operations,” Mr. Rubio said.

articles.title_orig: Russia strikes hospital in central Kyiv after SpaceX system falters again
articles.title_zh: Russia strikes hospital in central Kyiv after SpaceX system falters again
articles.content_orig:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy says speed restrictions on Starshield system made it harder for Ukraine to shoot down drones
Russia has attacked a hospital in the centre of Kyiv, close to several western embassies, after Volodymyr Zelenskyy said speed restrictions on SpaceX’s Starshield system had made it harder for Ukraine to shoot down enemy drones.
Three people were injured when a drone smashed into the National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopedics at 3am, hitting the second floor of the hospital and an adjoining 19th-century building.
Meanwhile, Russia claimed it had shot down nearly 1,200 Ukrainian drones overnight, one of the largest swarms sent by Kyiv. It reported that at least four people were killed in the southern region of Volgograd.
The blast in Kyiv blew out windows in nearby buildings including in the National Academy of Arts across the road. The six-storey hospital is located in the Shevchenkivskyi district, not far from the Danish and Romanian embassies, as well as cafes and a park popular with dog walkers.
Standing in the yard as smoke billowed from the burning building, and firefighters led dazed patients to safety, one witness, Oleksandr, said the attack had narrowly missed patients. “We were asleep when there was this massive boom. We all jumped out of bed straight away.
“There was glass all over the floor. People were running about … If it had hit a little further to the left it would have been much worse. We felt the shock wave.”
He added: “Targeting the wounded – that’s really low. Russia attacks everything. Where I live, high-rise blocks are being constantly hit by bombs. They don’t care where they drop them, or where they land.”
Russia has recently stepped up its strikes on Ukraine’s civilian infrastructure, hitting power plants, passenger trains and two bridges across the Dnipro river. Ukraine says the attacks are part of a campaign of terror, designed to make a weary population capitulate.
On Thursday, Zelenskyy said the Starshield system – operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX and overseen by the Pentagon – was again experiencing significant disruptions, after an unexplained slowdown last month.
He said some Russian aerial sorties had got through because Ukrainian interceptor systems that rely on the US satellite service could not reach the necessary speed to knock out enemy drones. Starshield is the Ukrainian military’s version of Starlink.
The White House has yet to explain why the service has been throttled for a second time, but it comes after intense US-led shuttle diplomacy this week, with Donald Trump seemingly pressuring Zelenskyy to make territorial concessions to Russia’s president, Vladimir Putin.
Trump’s emissaries, his son-in-law Jared Kushner and the real estate developer Steve Witkoff, met Putin in Moscow on Thursday. They then flew to Dublin to brief Zelenskyy on their talks, which came after trilateral negotiations on Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi.
Kremlin negotiators insist that Ukraine hand over four Ukrainian provinces, including cities and villages Russian troops have been unable to conquer. They are also calling for a new “security architecture” in Europe – a demand in effect that Nato go back to its pre-1997 posture, before eastern European nations joined the alliance.
At the same time, Moscow does not want European states to be involved in US-brokered talks to end the war in Ukraine. On Thursday, France’s president, Emmanuel Macron, said Europe had to take part since “US support” for Kyiv had ended.
“Without Europeans, there is no support for Ukraine,” Macron said. “At the end of the day, we will be the ones to define and decide for our future security as Europeans.”
Meanwhile, Russian strikes ⁠on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure ⁠overnight caused ⁠power ​outages in 12 ⁠regions, said deputy energy minister Artem ⁠Nekrasov. The ‌affected regions are ‌Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Zhytomyr, Kyiv, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Rivne, Sumy, Kharkiv, ‌Khmelnytskyi and Chernihiv.
“Energy workers ​are working at an intensified pace, ⁠but new attacks ​and constant ​air raid ​alerts ​are ‌complicating and delaying ​repairs,” ​Nekrasov said.
In Kyiv, the orthopaedic hospital’s director, Roman Derkach, said medical services had been temporarily suspended as a cleanup operation got under way. Thirty patients were taken to safety.

articles.title_orig: New candidate emerges to replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
articles.title_zh: New candidate emerges to replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
articles.content_orig:
Arm CEO Rene Haas joins ‘The Claman Countdown’ to break down the chipmaker’s record second-quarter revenue and surging demand from AI data centers.
Nvidia's Board of Directors has approached Rene Haas, the CEO of British chipmaker Arm, in its search for the successor to Jensen Huang, according to a report from the Financial Times.
The outlet reported Friday that Haas, who had led Arm since 2022, spent seven years working at Nvidia more than a decade ago and has a "strong relationship" with Huang and some of Nvidia's board members.
"It’s a no comment from us," Arm told FOX Business when asked about the report.
Huang resigned Thursday after Nvidia's board investigated his reported affair with a tech executive suspected of being a Chinese intelligence source. Huang is also alleged to have had extramarital relationships with two employees at Nvidia.
MEET NVIDIA'S NEW INTERIM CEO: THE FORTUNE AND RISE OF COLETTE KRESS
Jensen Huang, co-founder and former CEO of Nvidia. (Soeren Stache/picture alliance via Getty Images / Getty Images)
Nvidia said Thursday that Colette Kress, its current executive vice president and chief financial officer, has agreed to serve as interim CEO in the wake of Huang's departure.
"The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates," the company said.
NVIDIA CEO JENSEN HUANG RESIGNS AMID INVESTIGATION INTO RELATIONSHIP WITH ALLEGED CHINESE SPY
'The Big Money Show' panel analyzes the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation.
Nvidia described Jensen's contributions to the company as "profound."
"NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry," the company said.
"Kress has served as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA since joining the company in September 2013," it said, adding, "During her tenure, she has led the company’s finance organization and has played a key role in NVIDIA’s growth and evolution."
Rene Haas, CEO of Arm Holdings Plc, attends the annual Allen and Co. Sun Valley Media and Technology Conference at the Sun Valley Resort in Sun Valley, Idaho, on July 7, 2026. (Brendan McDermid/Reuters / Reuters)

"Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Harvey Jones, Chair of the Nvidia Board of Directors, said in a statement.
FOX Business' Elizabeth Claman contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
articles.title_zh: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
articles.content_orig:
China warned the United States on Friday against imposing additional controls on exports of semiconductors in the wake of the scandal surrounding AI chip giant Nvidia and its now-former CEO Jensen Huang.
China "has consistently opposed the abuse of export control measures, which disrupts the stability of global industrial and supply chains and serves no party's interests," foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told a regular press briefing when asked about calls from U.S. lawmakers to impose more limits on exports of chip equipment to China.
"China and the United States should work together to implement the important consensus reached by their respective heads of state and maintain the stable development of China-U.S. economic and trade relations," Mao said.
Jensen Huang — who resigned Thursday — has admitted to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. They're not related.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is under fire from critics asking whether his ties to Chinese companies and friendship with Jensen Huang contributed to a lack of oversight by the federal agency over billions in Nvidia AI chip sales, CBS News has learned . The Commerce Department did not respond to a request for comment.
During an interview on CNBC on Friday morning, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent placed the blame on Lutnick's Commerce Department for not including Megaspeed on what's known as the Entity List, which would restrict their ability to access U.S. technology products.
Bessent said that his department as well as the Defense Department, State Department and U.S. trade representative all supported adding Megaspeed to the list.
"They were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the Entity List for months," Bessent said, before referring to the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security. "Commerce BIS has the pen, and you will have to ask them about their internal processes."
According to a U.S. official, Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10.
Last month, the New York Times reported that about a year ago, President Trump was briefed on intelligence that suggested that Alice Huang was a Chinese asset and that she had grown close to Jensen Huang and the president decided not to do anything with the information.
House Speaker Mike Johnson said there's a growing consensus in Congress on further tightening controls on chip exports to China.
According to the Times , U.S. officials circulated a memo last spring citing intelligence alleging that Alice Huang was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, its main intelligence service.
Beijing has rejected the allegations and said on Thursday that they are a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" to stop China advancing in artificial intelligence technology .

articles.title_orig: Pope Leo visits the Peruvian city that has embraced him as one of its own
articles.title_zh: Pope Leo visits the Peruvian city that has embraced him as one of its own
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV has celebrated Mass near the Peruvian city where he made his name as a compassionate bishop who worked closely with poor and migrant communities.
The ceremony was held on Friday at a park in Pimentel, about 10km (six miles) from Chiclayo in northern Peru as part of his tour of Latin America.
The Vatican estimates more than 1.5 million people gathered to welcome the pontiff.
"Thank you for your affection, support and prayers," the Pope told followers.
"Especially for my health during this time of trial which, with God's help, I am overcoming," he added, referencing the surgery he had for lung cancer which took place just weeks ago .
Some of the crowd arrived 12 hours in advance to wait in vigil before the Mass began.
"We spent the night praying, alongside family, excited to welcome the Pope from Chiclayo," said Isa Orderique.
Many came from across Peru and even neighbouring countries to attend.
Merli Cruz Guerrero, from an area near the Ecuadorean border, travelled several hours by bus to attend. She also spent the entire night waiting.
Of all the events the Pope has attended so far during his visit to Peru, this felt particularly emotional.
The crowd fell into a hushed silence as the pontiff's motorcade approached.
They waited eagerly for his arrival despite spending long hours out in the open with the temperature pushing past 30C.
For many living here, the fact that the Pope worked extensively in this region before becoming the head of the Catholic Church has put them in the spotlight.
"The Pope has come home and Chiclayo is celebrating," said Lisbeth Díaz, a teacher who worked with Pope Leo when he served as the city's bishop between 2015 and 2023.
Peru is the longest stop on the first tour of Latin America by the pontiff , who was elected in May 2025.
The trip has also taken in Argentina and Uruguay, but his time in this country carries particular significance.
The Pope not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities.
Around Chiclayo, it is hard to meet anyone who doesn't claim to be a friend of the Pope or have a special anecdote about him.
Some recall how he would enjoy sampling Peruvian delicacies at El Trébol, a restaurant next to the city's cathedral. Others remember his love of tennis.
But for many it's the more serious moments of his time here, such as helping launch soup kitchens during the Covid-19 pandemic, or wading through deep waters on horseback when floods hit the area.
Several of these images are on display in a small museum dedicated to him at the entrance to the bishop's residence.
But for the city, and for a country that calls him the "Peruvian Pope", his return home means much more than a collection of photographs and anecdotes.
"It is the return of the man who brought Peruvians closer to the Church," said Samuel David Miranda Atoche, a local parish priest from Chiclayo who was ordained by the Pope back when he was still the bishop and known under his birth name of Robert Prevost.
And it is not just local people he connected with, according to Díaz, who came to Chiclayo from Venezuela.
"It was difficult for him to see so many migrants living on the streets," she added, recalling the time when large numbers of Venezuelans came through Chiclayo escaping the political and economic crisis in their home country.
"So, he got in touch with the migration authorities and coordinated with other organisations to speed up the paperwork needed for many of us to obtain legal residency and work permits."
Robert Prevost's time here as bishop also involved difficult decisions, such as having to deal with the controversy and scandal surrounding the dissolution of Sodalitium of Christian Life, a Peruvian Catholic organisation that had faced decades of sexual abuse allegations.
Santiago Roncagliolo, a Peruvian writer and journalist who has studied the Pope's life, believes his handling of that crisis earned him the favour of his predecessor, Pope Francis, and helped set him on the path to the papacy.
Father Miranda also stressed the role the now-pontiff played in bringing people together.
"If there is one thing Bishop Prevost worked for here," he added, referring to the Pope by his previous title, "it was unity".
That unity has been on display in the run up to the Mass, with the square in front of Chiclayo Cathedral filled with joyous celebrations for days.
Normally, 800,000 people live in the city and its surrounding area, but estimates say the Pope's visit has caused that to double.
Local businesses have been capitalising on the Pope's popularity to boost sales and hotels have sharply increased their nightly room rates.
But that didn't seem to put off the faithful who gathered for the Mass.
Shouts of: "The Pope is from Chiclayo!" echoed across the field during the event.
Their affection was clearly reflected by the pontiff.
"As I look at your faces, a prayer of thanksgiving to the Lord arises in my heart," he said from the stage, "for the blessing you have been and continue to be in my life."

articles.title_orig: Lutnick faces questions over Nvidia spy scandal. His sons’ firm has deep ties to the chipmaker
articles.title_zh: Lutnick faces questions over Nvidia spy scandal. His sons’ firm has deep ties to the chipmaker
articles.content_orig:
In late September, Cantor Fitzgerald hosted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and other top executives from the chipmaker for investor meetings in New York, according to a Cantor research report reviewed by CNBC.
The Wall Street firm liked what it heard.
"We continue to view NVDA as the best risk/reward in our coverage," Cantor analyst C.J. Muse and his colleagues wrote in a research report dated Oct. 3 that maintained a $350 price target and overweight rating on the stock.
Yet the firm formerly run by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and now led by his sons, Brandon and Kyle, reported a nearly 50% decline in the number of Nvidia shares it held between September 2025 and March 2026 , according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings that excludes options. Nvidia had been one of the largest stock positions reported in Cantor's filings.
The decline coincided with White House and U.S. intelligence officials pressing Lutnick to crack down on Megaspeed , a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence chips to China . Lutnick repeatedly resisted those efforts, according to Axios .
By the time Cantor hosted Huang in New York, Lutnick had also received a classified intelligence warning, according to Axios, about Huang's ties to a suspected Chinese spy and had appeared alongside the CEO at a G20 technology summit in North Carolina.
Even as Cantor pared back its Nvidia stake, it continued doing business across the chipmaker's AI empire. A CNBC review of securities filings, corporate announcements and Wall Street research found the firm has helped arrange billions of dollars in financing for Nvidia's business partners while maintaining close ties to the chipmaker's leadership.
Those ties have drawn fresh scrutiny following Huang's resignation Thursday and Axios' reporting that Lutnick repeatedly resisted a crackdown on companies suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, despite President Donald Trump authorizing new export restrictions on those companies for a third time on Nov. 5.
An ethics expert said the relationship between Lutnick and his former firm's investments may raise questions, given what the secretary knew about Nvidia.
Richard Painter , the former chief White House ethics lawyer for President George W. Bush and now a corporate law professor at the University of Minnesota said that while "there's no proof of" Lutnick sharing nonpublic information with Cantor Fitzgerald, "the appearance doesn't look great."
"His conversations with his sons better be about publicly available information," Painter told CNBC.
There is no evidence that Lutnick's sons had advance knowledge of the intelligence concerns, that changes in Cantor's reported holdings were tied to any warnings or that the firm's business interests influenced their father's decisions.
"Cantor has to date from time to time had only immaterial stand-alone proprietary positions in Nvidia, unlike the positions reflected in 13F filings which were entered into in the ordinary course of business in connection with client swap transactions, that are common in institutional markets," a Cantor spokesperson told CNBC.
Cantor declined to answer CNBC's other questions. The Commerce Department, the White House, Howard Lutnick and his sons did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment or detailed questions about the findings.
As scrutiny of Huang intensified, Cantor Chairman Brandon Lutnick was publicly praising the chipmaker's leadership. "Nvidia is one of the great companies on the planet, and they have an amazing leadership team," Brandon Lutnick told Fox Business on Wednesday.
Trump is standing by Howard Lutnick. A White House official told Reuters on Thursday that the president maintains "complete confidence" in the commerce secretary.
But cracks in the administration's unity emerged Friday, when Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC's "Squawk Box" that the Departments of Treasury, Defense and State and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative all "were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months."
Bessent pointed to Commerce as the department responsible for imposing the entity list, which identifies restricted businesses and other groups, adding, "You will have to ask them about their internal processes."
Nvidia was Cantor's second-largest reported stock position before Howard Lutnick left Wall Street to become commerce secretary in February 2025, behind only bitcoin investor MicroStrategy, now known as Strategy . At the end of 2024, the firm disclosed more than 3.5 million Nvidia shares worth $479 million, according to its quarterly securities filing .
That share count held steady through September 2025, but its value climbed 36% to $652 million, according to Cantor's quarterly securities filing , as the Trump administration moved over the summer to ease restrictions on Nvidia's H20 chip sales to China .
Over the following six months, however, the number of Nvidia shares Cantor reported holding fell by 49%, to 3 million in December and 1.78 million by the end of March 2026 , with their value dropping from $652 million to $310 million, according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings.
Pressure on Howard Lutnick was also mounting on Capitol Hill. Sens. Jim Banks, R-Ind., and Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., in March urged the secretary to suspend or reconsider Nvidia's export licenses after three people linked to Nvidia customer Super Micro Computer were indicted on charges of conspiring to smuggle AI chips to China.
"The Trump administration, I think, leaks like a sieve when it comes to non-public government information getting to various hedge fund guys," Painter said, though he stressed there is no evidence Howard Lutnick had shared such information with his sons.
The filings do not establish why Cantor's reported share count fell or whether its overall financial exposure to Nvidia declined. Nvidia’s stock had more than doubled from its April 2025 lows by late October, before retreating in the following months. The stock fell about 6.5% between the end of September and the end of March.
Cantor's reported Nvidia holdings remained near that lower level through June 30 , the latest quarter covered by public disclosures, at 1.81 million shares. Its next quarterly filing is due Monday.
Cantor has not publicly explained the decline.
Most of those shares were attributed to CF Secured , a Cantor brokerage subsidiary that uses stocks and derivatives to hedge customer transactions, according to its audited financial statements. Cantor also disclosed substantial Nvidia options positions during the time period CNBC examined, overwhelmingly skewed toward put options, which can protect against declines in the stock price.
As concerns about Huang escalated inside the Trump administration in May, according to Axios, Cantor was helping finance the expansion of one of Nvidia's newest business partners, securities filings show .
On May 7, Nvidia and Australia-based cloud computing provider IREN announced a five-year, $3.4 billion cloud computing contract and a strategic partnership giving the chipmaker the right to invest up to $2.1 billion in IREN.
"That's not a passive financial investment. Nvidia is a partner who wins as we deliver," IREN co-CEO Daniel Roberts told investors on the company's quarterly earnings call that day.
Five days later, as Trump headed to China aboard Air Force One, Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned him about Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, The New York Times reported on Tuesday. Huang, who had not initially been invited on the trip, joined the president's delegation during a refueling stop in Alaska.
Howard Lutnick had already been sent a highly classified intelligence memo detailing concerns about Huang's relationship, Axios reported.

articles.title_orig: Europe and Ukraine get a boost in peace talks, but Putin is playing for time
articles.title_zh: Europe and Ukraine get a boost in peace talks, but Putin is playing for time
articles.content_orig:
Russian president says he would target any foreign troops sent to Ukraine and refuses to soften territorial demands
Vladimir Putin warned US negotiators that Russia would target any foreign troops deployed to Ukraine, in a series of hardline remarks that came as the Ukrainian military faced renewed disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service.
During the talks at the Kremlin with the US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Thursday, the Russian president refused to soften his territorial demands, insisting on full control over four Ukrainian regions that Moscow claims to have annexed.
He also ruled out accepting the deployment of foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine , describing such a move as a “continuation of war”.
Putin’s comments appeared to severely dampen hopes that a peace deal could be within reach, after Volodymyr Zelenskyy said there was a “window of opportunity” to reach an agreement before the end of 2026.
The latest trip to Moscow by Witkoff and Kushner, who have made numerous visits to Russia, was partly aimed at securing European participation in future negotiations, according to two people familiar with the talks.
Speaking after the meeting, Witkoff confirmed that European representatives would join the next round of talks. “They’re our partners, and it’s important for them to be involved,” he told reporters as he boarded a plane leaving Moscow.
The US envoys will now travel to Dublin, Ireland, where they will meet Zelenskyy and debrief him on the Moscow meeting.
Andy Burnham, the British prime minister, said national security adviser Jonathan Powell would join the talks in Berlin.
Amid a flurry of diplomatic activity, including the recent talks in Abu Dhabi, the Kremlin appears to have succeeded in reframing negotiations over the war in Ukraine as part of a broader discussion about European security.
But Europe is wary of Russian attempts to focus discussions on a European security architecture, while Moscow continues to pound Ukraine with bombs and missiles.
The EU foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, told reporters: “We already have a European security architecture in place.” Kallas pointed to the cold war-era Helsinki accords and the Budapest memorandum , which guaranteed the territorial integrity of Ukraine. “The problem is that Russia is not keeping to those agreements, so right now the focus should be that Russia actually keeps to their obligations … and they don’t attack another country again.” Focusing on a European security architecture was a “distraction” without a ceasefire, she added.
Both Washington and Moscow have been urging European leaders to appoint a single representative to lead negotiations on their behalf.
“Once a representative is appointed, a chief negotiator authorised to speak on Europe’s behalf, there will be a four-way dialogue,” Putin said on Thursday.
EU leaders are due to discuss the issue of who speaks for Europe on Friday, but so far have declined to nominate one person to speak for the bloc. One EU official said the EU would be represented by its institutions when issues concerning the union were on the table, but played down any imminent appointment. They said: “Do I expect an agreement on a special representative? My answer is no, I don’t.”
Kallas suggested she – as the EU’s high representative for foreign and security policy – should represent the EU in talks, alongside António Costa, the president of the European Council.
More than 45 European leaders are meeting in Dublin for the European Political Community summit, a gathering that brings together nearly every country on the continent, apart from the leaders of Belarus and Russia.
The French president, Emmanuel Macron, played down the importance of having a single European negotiator, saying “the content determines the format”. “There is no more US support. So there [are] some mediations, fine,” he said, referring to the process led by Kushner and Witkoff. “But at the end of the day we will be the one to define and decide for our future security as Europeans.”
The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, said it was first necessary to get Putin to the negotiating table before deciding on a European envoy. Merz said: “It’s not about individuals. What matters is that Putin is prepared to hold talks.”
Meanwhile, Zelenskyy accused Musk’s Starlink satellite service of damaging Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russian drone attacks, after Ukrainian military officials reported new restrictions on the system.
According to Zelenskyy, Starshield, a military version of Starlink funded by the Pentagon, has for several days been subject to speed limits of 100mph (161km/h) along the frontline and in Russian-occupied territory.
Similar restrictions last month prompted confusion over who had ordered them, with Musk and the Trump administration pointing fingers at each other before the service was partly restored.
The latest restrictions had made it harder for Ukrainian forces to intercept Russia’s increasingly sophisticated jet-powered drones, Zelenskyy said, accusing the service of “helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine”.
Kyiv has contacted Washington to seek an explanation for the disruption, which Zelenskyy said appeared to be deliberate rather than a technical fault.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei aims to 'underpromise and overdeliver' as IPO valuation drops below $2T hopes
articles.title_zh: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei aims to 'underpromise and overdeliver' as IPO valuation drops below $2T hopes
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
A future of new scientific discovery where cancer, Alzheimer's, and heart disease are considered relics of the past, and artificial intelligence agents perform a growing number of complex tasks for humans safely.
Those were among the ambitions Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) CEO Dario Amodei laid out to JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) CEO Jamie Dimon Friday as the artificial intelligence startup prepares for one of the largest initial public offerings in history.
"We can have a much more beautiful world… It sounds starry-eyed. It sounds crazy. I really do believe it," Amodei said.
The remarks came during a livestreamed conversation hosted at JPMorgan's Manhattan headquarters, one of Anthropic's final stops this week in its Wall Street push to drum up investor demand for its IPO next week.
Amodei laid out a sweeping vision for the technology, from accelerating scientific discoveries and transforming medicine to deploying increasingly capable AI agents in fields such as robotics and cybersecurity.
He also pointed to the company's technology creating new markets.
"You're on an exponential of cognition, and as the exponential proceeds, new markets become possible," Amodei told Dimon.
But realizing those ambitions comes with enormous financial costs. Amodei described securing enough computing power to support Anthropic's growth without spending beyond its means as the company's "deepest business dilemma."
Asked by Dimon why Anthropic is going public now, the Princeton PhD pointed to the need for additional cash to help manage the uncertainty surrounding Anthropic's computing investments.
The company must commit to expensive infrastructure well before it knows how much demand its AI products will generate. Amodei said Anthropic generally purchases less capacity in advance than its growth projections might justify, supplementing it when demand exceeds expectations.
"We actually tend to buy on the low side," he said.
The IPO would provide an additional financial cushion as Anthropic balances those risks against its extraordinary growth ambitions.
"Just the more cash we have on hand, the more buffer we have between those two things," Amodei said, while suggesting the company isn't seeking to secure its highest valuation possible.
Anthropic wants to "underpromise and overdeliver," Amodei said.
Anthropic expects to price its offering Wednesday and begin trading Thursday, Nov. 19 , seeking to raise as much as $90.4 billion through its IPO and a concurrent private share sale at a valuation of approximately $1.4 trillion, according to the company's IPO website .
Just weeks ago, investors anticipated the company seeking a valuation as high as $2 trillion. Headwinds to financial conditions for the massive offering have been mounting in recent weeks as borrowing costs have climbed, political backlash over US data center development has won midterm election voters, and turmoil swirls around one of Anthropic's biggest chip suppliers and investors, Nvidia ( NVDA ).
In its IPO roadshow video earlier this week, Anthropic emphasized the durability of its revenue growth and its ability to use its own Claude technology to improve efficiency and control costs.
Anthropic has tapped JPMorgan to lead US retail sales in its IPO. Along with lead underwriting banks Goldman Sachs ( GS ) and Morgan Stanley ( MS ), it's one of 19 Wall Street lenders helping the company go public.
Evercore analysts estimated on Wednesday that the banks could earn roughly $395 million from the IPO, with JPMorgan taking home about $44 million in fees or about 0.1% of its fourth quarter earnings per share. That compares to $75 million in underwriting fees JPMorgan earned helping SpaceX go public.

articles.title_orig: You can adjust the position of the trackball on Keychron’s new wireless mouse
articles.title_zh: You can adjust the position of the trackball on Keychron’s new wireless mouse
articles.content_orig:
Computer mice ask people with very different hands to get along with the same fixed shape. Trackballs change how you move the cursor, but their ball can still sit just beyond a comfortable thumb reach. Keychron’s upcoming T1 HE Wireless Trackball Mouse adds an adjustment that addresses that mismatch, letting you reposition the ball without replacing the rest of the mouse around it.
The egg-shaped body keeps the arrangement familiar, with a broad palm area, two main buttons, and a scroll wheel above the ball. The white version adds gray button panels and pale blue accents, while black and translucent finishes offer different personalities. This is a right-handed layout, though, so moving the ball doesn’t turn it into an equally accommodating option for your other hand.
Underneath, adjusters let you shift the ball assembly sideways, forward and backward, or up and down. There’s roughly 3mm to 3.5mm of horizontal adjustment and 2mm to 2.5mm vertically. Those aren’t dramatic distances, but the intention is to bring the ball toward your thumb’s resting position, rather than asking you to keep stretching across the same fixed gap.
Once positioned, the mouse stays put while your thumb rolls the 1.34-inch ball to move the pointer. That could make more sense on a crowded desk than repeatedly clearing a path for a conventional mouse. The ball also lifts out for cleaning, giving you direct access to the socket underneath without making occasional cleaning a reason to dismantle the entire mouse housing.
The clicks have their own adjustment, courtesy of Keychron’s MagOptic switches. Optical mode provides one way to register a press, while magnetic mode lets you choose among 11 actuation settings and enables Rapid Trigger. In practical terms, you’re changing when a press registers and resets. You could select an earlier trigger point without needing to replace a switch or take the casing apart.
Those settings live in Keychron Launcher, a browser-based tool that also handles button remapping, shortcuts, and macros. Onboard memory keeps your configuration with the mouse when you change computers. There’s a connection requirement worth knowing: configuration uses a wired or 2.4 GHz link, not Bluetooth. You can avoid installing a dedicated desktop app, but you can’t do every adjustment over every connection.
Bluetooth can remember up to three devices, alongside the separate 2.4 GHz receiver option and wired USB-C operation. That gives a shared desktop and laptop setup several ways to connect without changing the mouse itself. Plugging in also lets you continue working while it charges, which is a useful fallback when the battery runs down halfway through whatever you were supposed to finish.
Notebookcheck reports a $59.99 international preorder price, with shipping expected around the end of the month. That remains an estimate, and adjustment alone doesn’t establish that this mouse will feel right in your hand. Still, it gives you something to change before giving up on trackballs altogether, particularly if a fixed ball position was what made your last attempt feel rather awkward.

articles.title_orig: China’s Military Purges Accelerate
articles.title_zh: China’s Military Purges Accelerate
articles.content_orig:
When China’s leader, Xi Jinping, endorsed the expulsion of dozens of disgraced officials at a recent Communist Party meeting in Beijing, one man stood out as a clear winner.
Taking his new place at the front of the meeting was Gen. Zhang Shengmin, the somber-faced enforcer of Mr. Xi’s purges inside the military. He had been promoted to the Politburo, the party’s top leadership council, the latest step in his improbable rise from low-profile inspector to a position second only to Mr. Xi in China’s military hierarchy.
General Zhang has been the principal overseer of Mr. Xi’s campaign to purify the People’s Liberation Army. His latest elevation signaled that the investigations, indoctrination drives and loyalty tests could continue for years, as Mr. Xi searches for officers he believes are irreproachably loyal, experts and officials said.
“Twist the blade inward, with strict measures to cure disorder,” China’s main military newspaper said after the party meeting that was held late last month, referring to the continued discipline campaign.
Three officials in Taiwan said they believed Mr. Xi’s loyalty campaign would keep the Chinese military focused on its own problems. That could hinder preparations for possible war over Taiwan, the self-governed island democracy that Beijing claims. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal assessments.
The leadership uncertainty comes as China’s military has continued to pressure Taiwan. Dozens of P.L.A. ships held unannounced drills in seas off the Chinese coast in recent weeks, with some, including a carrier strike group, still remaining, Joseph Wu , the secretary-general of Taiwan’s National Security Council, posted on X on Thursday.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia Stock Falls. It Faces One Big Threat in Life After Jensen.
articles.title_zh: Nvidia Stock Falls. It Faces One Big Threat in Life After Jensen.
articles.content_orig:
Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger are having a viral moment following Jensen Huang's departure as Nvidia CEO.
The AI chipmaker's founder stepped down Thursday following a scandal-filled week surrounding his personal life and relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.
The dayslong saga prompted many online commentators to share famous warnings from the former chairman and late vice-chairman of Berkshire Hathaway.
"My partner Charlie says: there's only 3 ways that a smart person can go broke -- he says 'liquor, ladies and leverage'" - Warren Buffet
                
                https://t.co/r9DOOfcnEZ
"My partner Charlie says that there's only three ways that a smart person can go broke: liquor, ladies, and leverage," Buffett said in a 2018 interview.
Charlie Munger seeing his “Liquor, Ladies, Leverage” quote being used more times in a 72 hours timeframe than any other time in human history https://t.co/NA5yNOOKdL
"Now, the truth is the first two he just added because they start with 'l' — it's leverage," Buffett added.
Charlie Munger once said liquor, leverage, and ladies are the downfall of men.
                
                Everyone thought AI would blow up over leverage, but no one was prepared for it to be women.
Huang admitted to being "unfaithful" to his wife following reports that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. He resigned as CEO after fresh claims that he had an affair with a subordinate.
Charlie Munger once said smart people go broke in three ways. Liquor, ladies, and leverage. https://t.co/6Ip17Gs9XH
Munger's caution about the risks of romantic entanglements has even been translated into other languages in recent days:
«Solo hay tres formas en las que una persona inteligente puede arruinarse: el alcohol, las mujeres y el apalancamiento».
                
                Charlie Munger https://t.co/rYsqGdBRM0
X users have also been relaying a classic piece of Buffett wisdom about how reputations are hard-won and easily lost.
“It takes 20 years to build a reputation  and 5 minutes to ruin it.”
                
                Buffett tried to tell them all and no one listened
Buffett has been issuing similar refrains for decades. He famously warned Salomon Brothers employees as their interim chairman in 1991: "Lose money for the firm, and I will be understanding. Lose a shred of reputation for the firm, and I will be ruthless."
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
Buffett has similarly told the managers of Berkshire subsidiaries: "We can afford to lose money—even a lot of money. But we can't afford to lose reputation—even a shred of reputation."
“It takes 20 years to build a reputation and five minutes to ruin it.”
                
                — Warren Buffett https://t.co/wZcic1lkQx
The legendary investor has also famously advised people to never do anything they wouldn't want printed on the front page of their hometown newspaper for all their friends and family to see.
Munger, Buffett's right-hand man for over 45 years, died at age 99 in November 2023. Buffett, now 96, stepped down as Berkshire's CEO at the end of last year, and as its chairman in September.
Berkshire stock has rallied strongly in recent days as investors have soured on AI stocks like Nvidia amid concerns about overinvestment and fears of a regulatory crackdown.
The Class B shares have jumped 13% in the past month to trade at $590, close to a record high. Nvidia stock is down 27% over the same period.

articles.title_orig: Before he was Pope Leo, he was their bishop. Now he’s back home.
articles.title_zh: Before he was Pope Leo, he was their bishop. Now he’s back home.
articles.content_orig:
LIMA, Peru — Pope Leo XIV made a triumphant return Friday to the Peruvian city of Chiclayo, where he served as bishop for eight years and was affectionately nicknamed “Padre Roberto.”
Leo arrived in a plane decorated with “#LeoXFliesHome” stickers and he was greeted with a sign at the airport bearing the same message. A small dance troupe performed before him as he stepped off the plane.
He will stay in the area until Sunday to lead eight events, including a private dinner with the priests who once reported to him as bishop.
The crowds greeting Leo in Peru’s fourth largest city will likely be smaller than the estimated 3 million or so who welcomed the pope when he arrived Wednesday in Lima, the country’s capital.
But their enthusiasm more than made up for their smaller numbers as the former Bishop Robert Prevost of Chiclayo returned to this coastal city of nearly 700,000 as the leader of the  Catholic Church.
As toured in an open-air popemobile at the Pampas de Pimentel, a vast desert plain just outside Chiclayo, the crowd erupted in cheers, many waving waved white-and-yellow Vatican flags.
Some had been waiting since last night to catch a glimpse of the pontiff, many of them forced to walk as lines of cars had blocked the roads where vendors sold hats, mini pope dolls and sweet Peruvian bread.
Maria Esther Chozo Reyes, 76, said she had taken a 12-hour bus ride from Lima and arrived Thursday afternoon before she camped overnight. “He knows the people of Chiclayo and he’s lived here, he’s made his mission here,” she told The Associated Press. “We really need his blessing.”
Thanking the people for their love and support, in his sermon Leo said it was a blessing to be in his former home.
“As I look at your faces, a prayer ⁠of thanksgiving to the Lord arises in my heart for the blessing you have been and continue to be in my life,” he said, adding that his lung cancer disgnosis and surgery to remove part of one lung exactly a month ago had been a time of trial.
Leo’s sojourn to Chiclayo is midway through the final leg of his 12-day visit to South America , a historic trip that included stops in Argentina and Uruguay. And it’s the most sentimental part of his journey.
For while Leo was born in Chicago and English is his mother tongue, the first words he uttered from the balcony of St. Peter’s Basilica was a shoutout in Spanish to his “beloved Diocese of Chiclayo.”
During his time in that city, Leo often repeated a joke: “Chicago, Chiclayo, what difference is there? Only one letter.”
Setting aside the fact that it’s actually two letters, Leo quickly became a beloved figure in Chiclayo by championing social justice issues, embracing the poor and venturing into the local prison to say Mass.
During the pandemic, Leo endeared himself to many by launching a fundraising drive to raise money for a badly-needed oxygen production plant.
When Cyclone Maku hit the area in March 2023, Leo was photographed wading through the floodwaters to get supplies to the destitute and distributing food at soup kitchens.
At Christmastime, Leo would drive a pickup truck laden with gifts into remote villages around Chiclayo and join family celebrations.
Leo spent two decades as a missionary, priest and finally as a bishop in Peru and became a citizen in 2015. During his two decades in the country, he was also a strident critic of then- Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori’s authoritarian regime .
On Thursday, Leo delivered a speech while sitting beside Fujimori’s daughter, recently-elected Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori, at Lima’s Gran Teatro Nacional performing arts center.
Leo urged the country’s leaders to cultivate honesty and integrity to strengthen public trust --- and called on officeholders to listen to their constituents.
“Today I understand how much of this land remains with me and how much of my own story also belongs to you,” Leo said.
There was thunderous applause when Leo referred to Peru as “my homeland.”
And Leo appeared to have tears in his eyes as he sang the Peruvian national anthem along with a children’s choir.
Claudio Lavanga reported from Lima and Corky Siemaszko from New York.
Claudio Lavanga is Rome-based foreign correspondent for NBC News.
Corky Siemaszko is a senior reporter for NBC News Digital.

articles.title_zh: China’s top diplomat calls for expanding cooperation in meeting with South Korean minister
articles.content_orig:
BEIJING, Nov 13 (Reuters) – China is willing to expand cooperation with South Korea in traditional and emerging sectors including ​artificial intelligence and biomedicine, Foreign Minister ‌Wang Yi said on Friday.
• In a meeting with his South Korean counterpart Cho Hyun, Wang said the two countries are “close neighbours that cannot be ‌moved ​away” and “maintaining good-neighbourliness and ⁠friendship is the right ⁠choice for both sides,” according to a statement released by China’s Foreign Ministry
• The South Korean diplomat is on a ​two-day visit to China starting Friday
• China-South Korea relations were “back onto the right ⁠track” after their leaders’ ⁠exchanges since late last year, Wang ​said
• Ties soured under Yoon Suk Yeol, the ​predecessor of South Korean President Lee ‌Jae Myung, who drew Seoul closer to Washington and Tokyo
• Lee, who took office in June 2025, has sought to restore ⁠relations, hosting Chinese President Xi Jinping in Gyeongju in late 2025 and making a state visit to ⁠China in ‌January
• China is willing to ⁠further enhance mutual trust with ​South ‌Korea and expand their common interests, ​Wang said
• ⁠Next week, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung will visit China and attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ meeting in Shenzhen
(Reporting by Shi Bu and Ryan Woo; Editing by ​Xevi Fontdegloria)

articles.title_zh: Nvidia’s stock is on a losing streak not seen in 14 years. What comes next?
articles.content_orig:
Stocks slumped on Friday, led by the chip makers caught in the swirl of Nvidia’s leadership turmoil, at the end of another volatile week for the market that, nonetheless, remained on course for its best week in months.
The S&P 500 is on track to rise roughly 2 percent for the week, which would be its best weekly performance since early August. That would come despite a 0.7 percent decline on Friday, capping a week that swung from gains to losses and back multiple times.
The Nasdaq Composite is up roughly 1.5 percent for the week, even after a fall on Friday.
The moves mark an end to weeks of losses in which concerns about a slowdown in the growth of the artificial intelligence industry weighed on the market and prompted sharp sell-offs in many of the tech companies that have led the market higher in recent years.
Friday’s sell-off, however, underscored earlier analyst warnings of the likelihood of more volatility to come, even if many still expect the market to rally through the end of the year.
“The market is in an incredibly good position to move higher,” said Mark Hackett, chief market strategist for the investment management arm at Nationwide, an insurance company. “Once you get through the news-driven sentiment, you can get back to focusing on fundamentals. That is hopefully what we are seeing.”
The market was on edge after revelations that Mr. Huang, a standard-bearer for the A.I. revolution , had engaged in an extramarital affair with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy.

articles.title_orig: Police investigating David Walliams over alleged serious sexual offences
articles.title_zh: Police investigating David Walliams over alleged serious sexual offences
articles.content_orig:
The Metropolitan Police has launched an investigation into David Walliams over reports of "alleged serious sexual offences".
It comes after ITV News and the Guardian published reports alleging that Walliams had been accused of sexual misconduct by several women.
The Met said that the allegations being investigated are separate from those reported by ITV and the Guardian, but as "part of their investigation, detectives are also proactively reviewing that reporting to establish whether there is any evidence of offences".
When those allegations were first reported, Walliams said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".
In a statement released on Friday, the Met said it had "received a number of allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving a man now in his 50s".
"Those who have come forward are being supported by specialist officers," the statement added.
Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney said: "We would encourage anyone who has been the victim of a sexual offence to come forward and speak to us, no matter when it happened.
"We know reporting allegations of this nature can be daunting, but specialist officers are on hand to provide support, answer questions and guide you through the process."
Allegations against the entertainer and children's author were published after he lost a legal bid to stop claims against him being made public by the media.
Some of the women in the investigation accused Walliams of "grooming" them when they were teenagers.
One now characterises her alleged encounter with Walliams at 15 years old as a "sexual assault". Walliams strongly denied he had any sexual contact with the girl.
He said he rejected any allegations of criminal activity and that he has never engaged in the grooming of young women.
The Guardian and ITV News said that several of the women, who do not know one another, allege they were targets of unwanted sexual advances from Walliams.
The investigation also claimed Walliams had a sexual relationship with at least one junior employee at publisher HarperCollins, and pursued another.
Other women alleged inappropriate behaviour at ITV's Britain's Got Talent, such as inviting girls and young women to his dressing room.
In a letter addressed to journalists working on the ITV and Guardian investigation, Walliams wrote: "Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.
"I realise I did not always take people's feelings properly into account. That is something I regret.
"And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did."
He added: "I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me."
Walliams shot to fame in the early 2000s with BBC sketch comedy Little Britain, served as a judge on ITV's Britain's Got Talent and launched a best-selling series of children's books.

articles.content_orig:

Federal traffic safety regulators are warning owners of more than 720,000 BMW automobiles to park outdoors because of an issue that could cause the cars to catch fire.
BMW said on Friday that it will recall 720,796 vehicles due to fire dangers when parked with engines shut off.
The affected models were initially recalled in 2024 to address a water pump problem and they will require a second fix, according to the agency.
“If you have one of these vehicles, you should park your vehicle outside and away from buildings and other vehicles until the vehicle is repaired,” NHTSA warned.
“An improperly sealed electrical connector on the water pump may be exposed to water and short circuit, increasing the risk of a fire.”
The automaker is currently developing a solution and has identified 10 fires potentially connected to the defect that happened after cars underwent the 2024 recall service. It is not aware of any crashes or injuries, federal regulators said.
The fix will be free at a BMW dealership when available.
• 2014-2016 BMW 2 Series coupe
• 2014–2016 BMW 3 Series sportswagon
• 2014-2016 BMW 328xi Gran Turismo
• 2014-2016 BMW 4 Series convertible
• 2014-2016 BMW 4 Series coupe
• 2015-2016 BMW 2 Series convertible
• 2015-2016 BMW 4 Series gran coupe
• 2016-2018 BMW X5 xDrive40e
Letters to owners about the issue are expected to be mailed beginning Dec. 25, 2026. Anyone with questions is urged to contact BMW’s recall hotline at 800-525-7417 or NHTSA’s Vehicle Safety Hotline at 888-327-4236.
Affected vehicle identification numbers and license plate numbers will also be searchable on NHTSA.gov/Recalls beginning Dec. 25, 2026.

articles.title_orig: US Wholesale Inflation Picks Up to Fastest Pace Since 2022
articles.title_zh: US Wholesale Inflation Picks Up to Fastest Pace Since 2022
articles.content_orig:
Wholesale prices increased less than expected in October, but inflation pressures persisted and the Federal Reserve is likely still on target for an interest rate increase soon.
The producer price index , which measures the prices domestic producers get for their products before they reach the consumer, rose a seasonally adjusted 0.3% for the month, against the Dow Jones consensus for a 0.4% increase, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Friday.
Stripping out food and energy, core PPI posted a 0.3% gain, meeting expectations.
On an annual basis, headline PPI accelerated 6.5%, up 0.2 percentage point for the highest annual rate since November 2022.
The report comes just a few weeks ahead of the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting, Dec. 8-9. Markets are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point increase in the central bank's key overnight borrowing rate, with slight odds that the Federal Open Market Committee might opt for a half-point hike.
Stock market futures added to gains following the release while Treasury yields were mixed.
Earlier this week, the BLS reported that inflation at the cash register was hotter than expected.
The headline consumer price index saw a 0.4% increase in October while core was up 0.3%, both 0.1 percentage point higher than expected. Because of the government shutdown in October 2025, the BLS couldn't collect some data and refrained from putting out a 12-month inflation figure for CPI.
However, the figures showed that the Fed remains a good distance from its 2% inflation goal.
"Today's PPI data – which shows some signs of improving, albeit still too-high – is unlikely to change the Fed's approach in December because the CPI data was already outside their comfort zone," said Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer for Northlight Asset Management.
Moreover, policymakers are beginning to worry that inflation generated by the Iran war and higher fuel prices, along with President Donald Trump's tariffs, are beginning to spread through the economy. The Fed generally would look through such price pressures as temporary, but the breadth of inflation could indicate that inflation is becoming more entrenched.
"We've had some signs of trouble now for several months in a row," Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said in a CNBC interview Friday. "If you look at how broad-based the inflation is, it's not just that we're above the target and have been for some time. It's that in categories that are not driven by oil prices and not driven by tariffs, you're still seeing stalled progress and in some cases going the wrong way."
Stripping out food, energy and trade services, PPI saw an increase of 0.5% in October.
Goods prices increased 0.5% in October, with more than 60% of that move driven by goods excluding food and energy, which actually saw a 0.1% decrease. On an annual basis, the goods index jumped 10.2%, the biggest 12-month surge since October 2022.
Final demand services prices increased 0.2%, most of which was linked to transportation and warehousing services, and within that category a 3.9% gain in truck transportation of freight.
"We've been above 2% for almost six years, and while it sometimes we were making progress, lately we're not making any progress, and if anything, it's going the wrong way," Goolsbee said. "Inflation is rising; it's proved far more persistent than we predicted at the beginning from the supply shocks."
Other items in the PPI report also showed multiyear gains. Prices for intermediate processed goods soared 14.6% from October 2025, the biggest annual gain since July 2022. Intermediate prices for services posted a 6.9% increase, the most since November 2022.
